chapters.title: Do Things that Don't Scale
chapters.text: Founders often start with narrow, manual loops before they can afford robust automation. In the early months, direct outreach creates momentum and reveals hidden assumptions. https://example.com/ds [1] Teams that embrace this pattern can discover segments that product analytics misses. They learn language from customers, adapt onboarding, and fix edge cases quickly. Repeated direct support builds trust and generates the evidence needed for future system design.

chapters.title: Founder Mode
chapters.text: Some organizations need a temporary operating style where leaders intervene deeply across boundaries. This does not replace delegation forever, but it can reset quality when coordination breaks down. https://example.com/fm [7] In this mode, context transfer must be deliberate and explicit, because speed without shared intent creates expensive rework. Once alignment improves, teams can move back toward distributed ownership with stronger interfaces and tighter feedback loops.
